house: The battle for control of the U.S. House of Representatives in 2026 appears to favor the Republican Party, though a significant number of toss-up races indicate a competitive landscape. While Democrats have a path to victory, it relies heavily on winning a disproportionate share of these highly contested districts. The current projections suggest Republicans are better positioned to secure the majority.
senate: The battle for the Senate in 2026 appears to favor Republicans, who are projected to hold a comfortable lead in non-toss-up races. Democrats face an uphill battle, needing to sweep the competitive races and flip at least one Lean Republican seat to gain control. The current landscape suggests a challenging cycle for the Democratic party.
governors: The 2026 gubernatorial elections feature 36 races, with Republicans currently holding a slight edge in projected non-toss-up wins. The battle for control will largely hinge on the outcomes of three highly competitive toss-up races, alongside several lean and likely contests. While neither party is projected to achieve a dominant majority, Republicans appear to be in a stronger position to maintain or slightly expand their current gubernatorial footprint.
